summary: Live tracking (WebSockets + driver-side app) fully verified end-to-end. Backend: added /app/backend/tests/test_live_tracking.py (8 tests, all pass in 8s). (1) Real geocoding via Google — POST /api/bookings with 'Connaught Place, New Delhi' + 'India Gate, New Delhi' returns numeric pickup_lat/lng≈(28.6304,77.2177), dropoff_lat/lng, and driver spawned ~1-2 km from pickup. GET /api/bookings/{id} echoes all six coords. (2) WebSocket /api/ws/tracking/{id}: on connect sends type='snapshot' with status + 6 coords; subsequent messages within 4s have type='location' with driver_lat/lng moving demonstrably closer to pickup (Euclidean distance decreases across ticks). (3) Opened a WS then PATCHed status to 'assigned' via a second HTTP call → a type='status' message with status='assigned' is broadcast to the socket within ~1s. (4) PATCH to 'picked_up' snaps driver to pickup coords (|Δ|<1e-6); PATCH to 'delivered' snaps driver to dropoff coords. (5) Simulator loop tolerates legacy doc (id='legacy-1' from iter_5) with null coords — /api/bookings returns 200, no crashes in backend.err.log during 8+ minutes of test run. Public WSS URL wss://vehicle-booking-app-21.preview.emergentagent.com/api/ws/tracking/{id} works — ingress DOES upgrade WebSockets (so frontend LIVE badge lights up in the preview URL — no infra note needed). Frontend (390x844): created a real booking via API, then loaded /tracking/{id} → live-map testID present, LIVE badge shows green dot + text 'LIVE' after ~3s. Header DRIVER button (testID='open-driver-view') navigates to /driver/{id}. Driver screen renders DRIVER MODE title + '// SIMULATOR' subtitle on yellow bar, driver-live-map testID visible showing pickup pin + driver truck marker + dashed route to dropoff, driver-status pill shows 'SEARCHING'. Sticky advance-status-button labels correctly evolved: 'ACCEPT & DEPART →' (searching) → 'GOODS PICKED UP →' (assigned) → 'DELIVERED →' (picked_up) → 'JOB COMPLETE' terminal state. Each tap PATCHes backend and status pill + button label update within 2s. call-sender-button and call-receiver-button both visible in [ CONTACTS ] card. Regression: BookingDetailsSheet → CONFIRM → /tracking/{id} flow still works (was re-validated in iter_5, no code changes here that could regress). Success: 100% backend (8/8 new tracking + 16/16 iter_5 = 24/24 relevant tests). Frontend 100% for tracking+driver flows. Pre-existing test_api.py (older payload schema) has 5 unrelated failures — NOT part of this iteration's scope.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents'. Non-blocking, from library internals. Ref: browser console during any screen render.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:277-287 driver spawn — offset_lat/lng nudged to >=0.008 deg (~0.9 km) if too close; sound guarantee that the driver does not spawn on top of pickup pin.
server.py:346-351 snap-on-status is idempotent and only fires if pickup/dropoff coords exist — safe for legacy docs.

server.py:402-435 simulator loop: 500-doc cap, skips docs missing any of the 4 required coords, broadcasts type='location' — clean design. `await asyncio.sleep(2)` outside the try/except so a burst of DB errors would still throttle, good.

server.py:370-395 WS handler awaits receive_text() in a while-True to keep socket alive but never dispatches client messages — this is intentional (unidirectional stream). WSManager set-based storage safely deduplicates and cleans up on disconnect.
useTrackingSocket.ts:20-56 auto-reconnect after 3s + closed flag guard against setState-after-unmount is well-formed. wsRef.current is nulled on close before the timer — no double-connect race.
tracking/[id].tsx:86-110 Haversine auto-advance uses 0.15 km (150 m) threshold and swallows API errors so a transient PATCH failure just retries on next WS tick — resilient.

LiveMap.tsx:126-136 web path uses srcDoc iframe (no leaflet in bundle), native path uses react-native-webview — clean platform split. postMessage 'map-ready' handshake correctly buffers pending payload until iframe is loaded.
driver/[id].tsx:59-72 advance() uses busy flag to prevent double-taps — good UX for slow networks.

Note (not a blocker): backend does not auto-advance status server-side; it relies on the client-side Haversine or driver-side tap. If both client & driver page are closed while simulator keeps ticking, status will remain 'searching' forever. This matches design intent per the review note but is a known product decision.
